justifications.functional_suitability: Claims Web Application (Claim Submission Feature, Adjuster Workspace) covers R-01/R-02; Feature Flag Manager, Claim Type Adapter and Dual-Write Router support per-type migration (R-03). Gaps: no distinct broker interface, payment gateway link unconnected to any container, Data Access Layer undefined.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Adjuster Workspace uses TanStack Query caching, and Service Bus plus Batch Window Throttler decouple the 5 s mainframe. Container Apps scale. Gaps: no server-side cache or read model for mainframe data, no quantified load figures, cold-load first-view not addressed.
justifications.compatibility: Anti-Corruption Layer with Mainframe Translation Adapter, mTLS over ExpressRoute and Service Bus fits the legacy interface. Entra ID via OIDC/MSAL, Payment Gateway via REST. Gaps: mainframe interface-change limit not explicitly handled, no concrete mainframe protocol detail (AMQP vs TCP inconsistent).
justifications.usability: Routing & Shell Component with WCAG 2.1 AA, Claim Submission Feature with multi-step forms and local storage resilience, and an Adjuster Workspace. Gaps: brokers have no dedicated features, no UX feedback for async status, a single shared web app for all groups.
justifications.reliability: Idempotency & Outbox Processor, Polly in Rate Limiting & Resilience Component, local fallback cache, Break-Glass Workflow, Claim Provenance & Audit Registry for fallback, Service Bus queuing. Gaps: no multi-region HA or backup/DR, dual-write consistency risk, unclear rollback data reconciliation.
justifications.security: Entra ID SSO via MSAL and Authentication & Authorization Middleware, memory-only tokens, WAF, mTLS, Key Vault with Automated Rotation Service, TDE, Row-Level Security, Dynamic Data Masking, SQL Ledger audit. Gaps: no explicit role-based authorization model; duplicated audit components.
justifications.maintainability: Clear container decomposition: BFF, Claims Processing Service, Anti-Corruption Layer, Claim Type Adapter strategy pattern, GitOps Deployment Pipeline, and feature flags support one-day rollback. Gaps: inconsistent component diagrams (Claims Database duplicated, undefined Data Access Layer), Security & Observability container is an overloaded catch-all.
justifications.portability: Hybrid Azure plus on-prem is addressed via ExpressRoute, mTLS and Bicep/Terraform in GitOps Deployment Pipeline; containerised Claims Processing Service. Gaps: heavy Azure-specific services (Functions, Cosmos DB, App Configuration) with no abstraction, and the team's limited cloud experience is unaddressed.

sensitivity_points: No read model explicitly synced from mainframe
tradeoffs: Local SQL copy versus consistency with mainframe
PERF-01.justification: TanStack Query caching and a local Azure SQL store can plausibly keep loads under 2 s. But no mechanism is shown for fetching mainframe-only data, such as a read model or timeout fallback; Polly is only generic. Cold loads remain a risk.

sensitivity_points: Throttler is only a Service Bus queue
tradeoffs: Asynchronous acceptance versus delayed mainframe visibility
Queue buffering versus backlog after the window
PERF-02.justification: Submissions are persisted in Azure SQL and queued through Service Bus, with a throttler honoring the batch window. Scalable Container Apps absorb 5x peaks. Throttling logic details and backlog drain are unspecified, but the mechanism clearly protects the mainframe.

sensitivity_points: Ordering and replay after the window
AVAIL-01.justification: Submissions are stored locally, outbox messages are persisted transactionally, and Service Bus holds them until the window closes. Idempotency prevents duplicates on replay. The outbox-to-queue relay isn't explicitly drawn, but the pattern is clearly present.

AVAIL-02.justification: Transactional outbox, deduplication keys, and a provenance registry track routing state, supporting reconciliation without loss or duplication. However, a dual-write router is risky, and no explicit reconciliation job or mainframe-side idempotency is described.

sensitivity_points: Mainframe interface change quota of one per quarter
tradeoffs: Per-claim-type isolation versus more adapters to maintain
Feature flag flexibility versus configuration risk
MOD-01.justification: A strategy-pattern adapter, feature flags, canary routing, and a break-glass workflow support per-type migration and switch-back within a day. Data resynchronization on rollback to the mainframe isn't detailed, and the mainframe interface change is not explicitly addressed.

sensitivity_points: Mainframe-specific logic leaking into the BFF or UI
tradeoffs: Anti-corruption layer overhead versus a clean cutover
Retaining sync components versus decommission effort
MOD-02.justification: UIs talk only to the BFF and the Claims Processing Service, with the mainframe isolated behind an anti-corruption layer. Removing it leaves the UIs untouched, and Azure SQL is ready as the system of record. Historical data migration is not described.

tradeoffs: Fine-grained authorization versus performance and complexity
SEC-01.justification: JWT validation, Row-Level Security, and audit logging exist, but no broker-customer relationship authorization is defined. Denial recording is only implied via the audit logger, and nothing ensures enforcement in the mainframe, so access in both systems is not guaranteed.

sensitivity_points: Mainframe credentials not tied to AD
tradeoffs: Short token lifetimes versus more reauthentication
SEC-02.justification: OIDC with Active Directory and memory-only tokens revoke access to the new platform quickly if token lifetimes are short. But the mainframe access path uses mTLS service identities and no AD-linked mainframe user deprovisioning is shown, so removal from both systems within 15 minutes is unaddressed.
